section: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - structure, jurisdiction, working; Central Vigilance Commission
subsections: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Lokayukta in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A constitutional authority that adjudicates corruption cases
A police agency exclusively empowered to investigate disproportionate-assets cases
A statutory ombudsman under the 1983 Act that receives citizens’ complaints, conducts inquiries and makes recommendations
A central department exercising disciplinary control over all State employees
accepted.x: The Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta constitute a statutory ombudsman institution under the 1983 Act. It receives citizens’ complaints, conducts inquiries and makes recommendations.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the statutory ombudsman from the police investigating agency and the vigilance body.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

accepted.s: The report of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta is submitted to the
o: Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court
accepted.x: The Lokayukta reports to the Governor. It does not function as a police agency or as a department directly subordinate to the Chief Minister.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who receives the report?’ approach to separate constitutional authorities from statutory bodies.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the State Vigilance Commission in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was set up from 1964 on the pattern of the Central Vigilance Commission.
2. It advises on vigilance and disciplinary matters in government departments.
3. It is primarily a police investigating agency for trap cases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because investigation of Prevention of Corruption Act offences, including trap cases, is the role of the Anti-Corruption Bureau.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong statement by separating an advisory vigilance body from a police investigating agency.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the principal role of the Anti-Corruption Bureau in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Receiving complaints and submitting recommendations to the Governor
Investigating offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases
Advising departments on disciplinary matters without investigating offences
Exercising superintendence over the Central Bureau of Investigation in all cases
accepted.x: The Anti-Corruption Bureau is a police investigating agency that investigates Prevention of Corruption Act offences, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases.
accepted.tq: Match the agency with its operational function rather than its broad anti-corruption label.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

accepted.s: As of April 2026, the Andhra Pradesh Anti-Corruption Bureau was headed at the Inspector General level by
accepted.x: R. Jayalakshmi headed the Andhra Pradesh Anti-Corruption Bureau at the Inspector General level as of April 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the designation and date together to avoid confusing current office-holders with former office-holders.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

accepted.s: A major institutional weakness of many Lokayuktas is that they
o: have no independent investigating wing and depend on the State police or Anti-Corruption Bureau
submit all reports directly to Parliament
have no statutory basis in any State
accepted.x: Many Lokayuktas lack an independent investigating wing and therefore depend on the State police or the Anti-Corruption Bureau for investigation.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional-design distinction between inquiry, investigation and prosecution.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lokayukta — Police investigating agency for trap cases
State Vigilance Commission — Advisory body on vigilance and disciplinary matters
Anti-Corruption Bureau — Body submitting reports to the Governor as an ombudsman
Lokayukta — Department exercising disciplinary control over departments
accepted.x: The State Vigilance Commission advises on vigilance and disciplinary matters. Trap investigations belong to the Anti-Corruption Bureau, while the Lokayukta is the statutory ombudsman.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional-function pair and eliminate swapped roles.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. First Lokpal Bill introduced
B. Sweden established the first ombudsman
C. Maharashtra established the first Lokayukta
D. First Lokpal appointed in India
accepted.x: Sweden’s first ombudsman dates to 1809, the first Lokpal Bill to 1968, Maharashtra’s first Lokayukta to 1971, and India’s first Lokpal appointment to 2019.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two middle events by year.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the year or place associated with the first institution?
accepted.x: Sweden had the first ombudsman in 1809. Odisha enacted the first Lokayukta law in 1970, Maharashtra established the first Lokayukta in 1971, and India appointed its first Lokpal in 2019.
accepted.tq: Check whether the option confuses the first law, first office and first office-holder.

accepted.s: Who is identified as the present Chairperson of the Lokpal from 2024?
accepted.x: A.M. Khanwilkar is identified as the present Chairperson of the Lokpal from 2024.
accepted.tq: Use the year marker to distinguish the current Chairperson from the first Lokpal.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the history of Lokayukta institutions is correct?
o: Maharashtra enacted the first Lokayukta law in 1970, while Odisha established the first Lokayukta in 1971.
Odisha enacted the first Lokayukta law in 1970, while Maharashtra established the first Lokayukta in 1971.
Sweden enacted the first Lokayukta law in 1970, followed by Maharashtra in 1971.
Andhra Pradesh established the first Lokayukta in India in 1970.
accepted.x: Odisha had the first Lokayukta law in 1970, whereas Maharashtra was the first State to establish a Lokayukta, in 1971.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the first law and the first established office.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the institutional status of Lokayukta laws:
1. Lokayukta laws are uniform throughout India.
2. Their powers are often advisory in nature.
3. Dependence on State police is a criticism of the institution.
4. Executive attempts to dilute their powers have been part of the criticism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is false because Lokayukta laws lack uniformity across States.
accepted.tq: Test the exception to a broad institutional claim: non-uniformity is a central criticism.

accepted.s: Which one of the following criticisms of the Lokpal institution is NOT correct?
o: The delay has been viewed as indicating political reluctance.
There was a five-year delay before the first Lokpal was appointed.
Inquiry and prosecution wings have remained fully staffed since the beginning.
A two-year vacancy occurred after the first Lokpal’s tenure or appointment period.
accepted.x: The inquiry and prosecution wings have not remained fully staffed; their continuing staffing problems are among the criticisms. The other statements describe reported concerns regarding delay and vacancy.
accepted.tq: Find the absolute reversal of a documented institutional weakness.

accepted.s: The Lokpal’s Inquiry Wing was set up under which provision?
o: Section 7 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act
Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act
Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act
accepted.x: The Lokpal set up its Inquiry Wing under Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act. Section 17A belongs to the Prevention of Corruption Act.
accepted.tq: Separate provisions by identifying the statute to which each section belongs.

accepted.s: A parliamentary standing committee observed in March 2026 that the Director of Inquiry and inquiry-wing staffing were
o: abolished after the first Lokpal appointment
still in process more than a decade after the Act
accepted.x: The parliamentary standing committee noted that the Director of Inquiry and inquiry-wing staffing were still in process more than a decade after the Act.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-status wording precisely; do not replace ‘still in process’ with ‘fully operational’.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act:
1. It concerns prior approval before investigation.
2. Justice K.V. Viswanathan upheld the provision only when approval is based on a binding opinion of the Lokpal or Lokayukta.
3. Justice B.V. Nagarathna held the provision unconstitutional.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The split verdict dealt with prior approval under Section 17A, including the binding-opinion qualification and the contrary view that the provision is unconstitutional.
accepted.tq: Retain the separate conclusions of the two judges instead of treating a split verdict as unanimous.

accepted.s: In the split verdict concerning Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, Justice K.V. Viswanathan and Justice B.V. Nagarathna respectively held that
o: Section 17A was valid without any approval; the Lokpal had no role
Section 17A was unconstitutional; prior approval was always mandatory
prior approval was valid only with a binding Lokpal/Lokayukta opinion; Section 17A was unconstitutional
both judges held Section 17A fully constitutional without qualification
accepted.x: Justice K.V. Viswanathan upheld prior approval only if it was based on a binding opinion of the Lokpal or Lokayukta. Justice B.V. Nagarathna held Section 17A unconstitutional.
accepted.tq: Map each judge to the precise holding rather than remembering only that the verdict was divided.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the distinction between the Central Vigilance Commission and the Lokpal in relation to the Central Bureau of Investigation?
o: The CVC has superintendence over the CBI generally in Prevention of Corruption Act cases, whereas the Lokpal has it only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has general superintendence, while the CVC acts only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has superintendence over the CBI in every Prevention of Corruption Act case.
Neither the CVC nor the Lokpal has any relationship with the CBI.
accepted.x: The CVC Act, 2003 gives the CVC superintendence over the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases generally. The Lokpal exercises such a role only in cases referred by it.
accepted.tq: Compare the scope words ‘generally’ and ‘only in cases it refers’.

accepted.s: The Delhi High Court set aside the Lokpal’s sanction order dated 12 November 2025 in which case?
o: The Section 17A reference concerning Justice Nagarathna
accepted.x: The Delhi High Court set aside the Lokpal’s 12 November 2025 sanction order in the Mahua Moitra case. The Supreme Court agreed to clarify the Lokpal’s sanction procedure.
accepted.tq: Match the judicial action with the specific case and date.

accepted.s: Which one of the following developments was associated with the Supreme Court in March 2026?
o: It appointed the first Lokpal of India.
It agreed to clarify the Lokpal’s sanction procedure after the Delhi High Court decision in the Mahua Moitra case.
It transferred all State Lokayukta inquiries to the CVC.
It abolished the Lokpal’s Inquiry Wing under Section 11.
accepted.x: Following the Delhi High Court’s decision in the Mahua Moitra case, the Supreme Court agreed to clarify the Lokpal’s sanction procedure in March 2026.
accepted.tq: Link the later judicial development to the earlier order and case instead of confusing it with the Section 17A verdict.

accepted.s: The annual report of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta for 2025 recorded which of the following?
accepted.x: The 2025 annual report recorded 3,654 disposals and recovery of ₹15.29 crore.
accepted.tq: Keep the count and monetary figure paired; the distractors reverse or alter one figure.

accepted.s: Which one of the following proposals has been suggested in debates concerning Lokayukta institutions?
o: Removal of all investigative functions from anti-corruption bodies
Constitutional status for the Lokayukta and a model Lokayukta Act
Replacement of the Lokayukta by the Central Vigilance Commission in every State
accepted.x: The criticisms and debates have included a suggestion for constitutional status for the Lokayukta and the adoption of a model Lokayukta Act.
accepted.tq: Identify the reform proposal rather than selecting an extreme abolition or replacement option.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: State Vigilance Commission — Set up from 1964 on the CVC pattern
accepted.x: Section 17A belongs to the Prevention of Corruption Act and concerns prior approval before investigation. The Lokpal Inquiry Wing is associated with Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act.
accepted.tq: Check the statute before accepting a section-number match.

accepted.s: A citizen submits a complaint against a public servant and seeks an inquiry followed by recommendations to the Governor. Which institution most directly fits this description?
o: Central Vigilance Commission exercising general superintendence over the CBI
accepted.x: The Lokayukta receives citizens’ complaints, conducts inquiries, makes recommendations and reports to the Governor. The ACB investigates criminal corruption offences, while the Vigilance Commission has an advisory role.
accepted.tq: Trace the complete chain—complaint, inquiry, recommendation and report—to identify the ombudsman.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP
